reviewerOrPass: Worker B, same AI, separate source-first pass
method: After freezing and replaying the record, reread the 2026-entry student curriculum, faculty and programme regulations, and the thesis catalogue. Recomputed the 135 EC major and 45 EC profiling space, checked the cohort-Annex versus summary discrepancy and recalculated advanced credits before and after the thesis. Reconsidered the published options using the underlying course evidence, including the differences between comparative policy, historical inquiry, market regulation and environmental governance. This is a separate same-AI pass.
findings: The English-taught 2026-entry degree totals 180 EC. The 135 EC major has eight first-year courses (60), three required methods courses (22.5), a thematic package (22.5), two advanced selections (15) and the thesis (15). The 45 EC profile is elective within faculty rules. Article 3.5.1 gives 90 EC for Annex 1 taught requirements, which conflicts with its enumerated courses, the 135 EC major cap in the same article, and the cohort-specific student curriculum. Annex 1 explicitly applies to this cohort, supplies 60 plus 22.5, and is independently corroborated by the detailed 2026-entry curriculum. That interpretation accounts for all 135 EC without fabricating an extra component. Annex 6 preserves older-cohort requirements separately. The selected welfare package and advanced philosophy and history choices follow official order. The advanced history title and the third methods title are provisional, so no unsupported content or exact equivalence is attributed to them.

The eight first-year courses precede the year-two methods and thematic work. Integrating Insights, Knowledge and Reasoning, both advanced electives and the thesis provide 45 advanced EC in the major. Year two contributes 30 advanced EC before the thesis. The current thesis catalogue requires programme enrollment and 15 advanced EC, and the thesis integrates two disciplines. Year three includes a thesis lab and final thesis together worth 15 EC; 45 elective EC includes at least 15 intermediate EC under the faculty EER. The programme page identifies 45 of 60 first-year EC for positive binding study advice. No assumed first-year elective, older skills course or extra thesis credit is inserted.

Welfare and public policy best fits the four-discipline common core and the illustrated thematic package. Ethics, political philosophy, agency and judgment frame normative questions; public economics examines taxation and social insurance; modern, gender and imperial history ground institutions in context; policy analysis and three forms of research methods support inquiry. Philosophy of mind, advanced calculus and behavioral economics were replaced in that plan with historical breadth, a historical research course and direct policy analysis. The market-regulation plan keeps economics and quantitative methods, including econometrics and behavioral economics, and adds constitutional and international law, EU law and EU politics. Together they distinguish it from the closest plan. The sustainability plan includes biodiversity and farming impacts, water management, climate science, energy transition and geospatial evidence, with policy analysis, public economics, ethics and climate justice. This supplies the substance for the official sustainability interests beyond generic environmental content. Democracy remains substantively represented in the closest plan through comparative institutions and democratic backsliding, political philosophy, modern history and policy. The fourth thematic package was considered and its interests are covered within the closest plan, with the available three slots occupied by distinct designs. The advanced external options lack full published topic details, and the integrated package and required two-discipline thesis have no directly equivalent UCR component.
